messages:
margo: Heads-up — seeing apiserver p90 jump in eu-west1 during the morning GPU attach window. correlates with a big spike in outbound proxy connections. p90 went from ~450ms to ~1.8s for ~15m.
ryan: any leader flips in etcd around that time?
samir: quick look — etcd leader stayed steady, but watch backlog increased. logs show a bunch of socket resets from the kube-proxy tier. snippet:
```
# at 2026-03-18T08:11:22Z
apiserver_request_latency_seconds{verb="LIST"} p90 = 1800ms
kube_proxy_conn_reset_total = +320
nat_snat_alloc_failures = +48
```
margo: interesting — NAT/SNAT failures match the times. we suspected NAT exhaustion when we saw mass rtx attach churn earlier, but this ties it to controlplane latency.
sre-oncall: infra-bot alerted at 08:09 — "proxy: snat pool exhausted eu-west1-primary" and rate-limited retries started piling on. infra-bot: @channel SNAT_POOL_EXHAUSTED region=eu-west1 pool=primary count=48
ryan: that will cause apiserver backpressure if kube-proxy can't maintain watch streams. are GPU attaches coming from worker autoscaler or from Dedicated onboarding jobs?
samir: looks like a mix — scheduled batch onboarding jobs + scale-up from ML team. cost note: those onboarding runs do allocate GPUs then run heavy image pulls, increasing concurrent egress.
margo: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) increase SNAT pool for eu-west1 2) throttle the onboarding job concurrency 3) route controlplane traffic via the control-plane-only NAT (we have a small spare pool)
ryan: agree. also we should consider tuning apiserver watch-cache / list burst handling — a heavy reconciling workload is making LIST calls spike. can we enable watch coalescing on the controller-manager for that cluster?
samir: controller-manager flags we can try: `--min-resync-period=15m` and bump `--leader-elect-lease-duration=45s` to reduce thrash. also, moving large batch jobs to a staging region during onboarding would help.
sre-oncall: implementing SNAT pool bump now, and I disabled two concurrent onboarding jobs (batch IDs: onboarding-34, onboarding-35). watching metrics.
(2m later) infra-bot: SNAT_POOL_INCREASED region=eu-west1 pool=primary new_size=256 :white_check_mark:
samir: after we increased SNAT and paused onboarding, watch backlog is dropping and apiserver p90 is trending back toward baseline. still keeping an eye on kube-proxy resets.
margo: action items: 1) infra: permanently increase control-plane SNAT capacity for eu-west1 (sre-oncall). 2) eng-runtime: add soft concurrency limit to onboarding job (samir). 3) product: schedule big onboarding outside peak window (margo). 4) follow-up: evaluate if we need a dedicated controlplane NAT or separate egress for heavy image pulls (ryan).
ryan: +1 on follow-up. also add a postmortem-lite if this recurs. quick ack :thumbsup:
sre-oncall: noted, will update runbook and close alert when stable.
margo: thanks everyone, keep updates in this thread if anything regresses.
